title: THE GUIDE · what you can say here, and what happens
kept_by: the kernel — the same words on every door; Fable keeps it current with each spoonful

sections.title: The chat
sections.lead: Type to the crew. A reply always arrives whole. Esc closes one thing at a time.

entries.say: what is the temperature outside?
entries.does: A thought: the librarian answers with its tools; every body it needs is asked.

entries.say: echo, say the word HERON once
entries.does: A name at the head sends the ask to that body alone.

entries.say: librarian, remember that I went to the trailer today
entries.does: The librarian keeps the words in the Record. Ask later: "what do you remember about the trailer?"

entries.say: between 9am and noon, what did I ask?
entries.does: Sets the time window the crew reads from; "since yesterday" works too.

entries.say: follow up on this by counting the asks
entries.does: A child of the origin last opened in the Analyzer.

entries.say: summon MITL
entries.does: The Master Mind In The Loop reads the canon and says what a change touches; every hold offers "expected impact?".

entries.say: export compliance for this session
entries.does: A table of every ask, act and reply with its chain of who acted for whom, signed by the kernel; two downloads beneath it, JSON and CSV.

entries.say: list my sessions · new session
entries.does: Your worldlines, newest first, each with its short version; a new session archives the old one — nothing is deleted.

entries.say: guide · help · ?
entries.does: This guide, opened to where you are.

sections.title: THE PANEL — the main window
sections.lead: The kernel drawn as a control room's panel. Geometry is architecture: every block sits where its declaration puts it and never moves. Light is operations: a fact on the feed lights a lamp or a rail segment, then fades. Colour is origin: amber a person's word, cyan a body's act, violet the kernel's own, red a watch or a hold. A quiet kernel is a dark, still panel. The panel knocks on no door by a clock: the roster, the stations and every lamp follow the feed — a body joining, refused, parked, its lease crossing the line.

entries.say: (click DESK · GROUND · GATEWAY · SHELF · MONITOR · ANALYZER)
entries.does: The kernel's six organs, always seated. A click opens the inspector in place: what it is, its self, what it serves, and one-click doors into the chat, the crew, the monitor or the analyzer.

entries.say: (click a station — planner · librarian · echo …)
entries.does: A crew seat. Solid = seated by its lease; dashed = declared, not seated; amber = parked by the kernel. The inspector shows its self, lease, life and last act; "scope the chat here" makes the chat speak to that body alone.

entries.say: (click a tool under the shelf)
entries.does: A tool the kernel governs. Its border says how consequential it is: plain routine, amber consequential, red grave. Retire or restore it from the inspector — a retire holds at the interlock.

entries.say: (click a row on the running board)
entries.does: The intention → objective → thought → action chain, live. A click opens that origin in the Analyzer.

entries.say: (click ARCHITECTURE · OPERATIONS · PERFORMANCE on the sill)
entries.does: Three soft toggles on one drawing, any combination. ARCHITECTURE shows the empty sockets and the tools; OPERATIONS the rails and the board; PERFORMANCE the numbers: under each organ its doors' p95 (how long the slowest one in twenty knocks took), under the GROUND the pool of lines to the ground (how many are busy, how many knocks wait for one), the outbox's age, the spend, the benches' depth, and THE DOORS row - every door this kernel answered in the last ten minutes, the slowest first, red past one second. A watch can stand on door_p95_ms, pool_busy or pool_waiting.

entries.say: (click FULL SCREEN on the sill, or press F)
entries.does: The panel alone, edge to edge, for a wide monitor: the ceiling, the tabs and the floor fold away, the browser goes full screen too, and on a wide display the drawing is scaled up to be read from across the room. The sill stays as the one thin bar - the toggles, CHAT, ANALYZER and the way out. Esc or F leaves it. Remembered in this browser.

entries.say: (click a marker chip — structural · quality · resiliency)
entries.does: Dims that group's rows on the board and the tape.

entries.say: (click ☀ or ☾ in the ceiling)
entries.does: The Daylight Glass: the same panel in daylight — paper, ink, bronze — or back to the night. Remembered in this browser; with nothing remembered, your system's own preference decides.

entries.say: (watch the presence track · a tool's lamp · the scheduler's track)
entries.does: A lease lapsing lights the presence track red and the station goes dashed within five seconds; seated again, violet. A tool hop lights the tool's lamp cyan under the shelf and the dispatcher's track toward it. A duty waking on its clock lights the scheduler's track toward the runner. A lever the kernel pulls lights the monitor and the intent track toward the body it acts on — red when it is held at the interlock for your word.

sections.title: The kind of an ask
sections.lead: The chip under the composer reads the kind from your words; one click flips it.

entries.say: thought: …
entries.does: One answer, now.

entries.say: objective: …
entries.does: Work the crew owns until it is done; the Analyzer shows it under its origin.

entries.say: keep this world resilient: when a watch goes red, get it green
entries.does: An intention — a standing purpose that wakes on what it watches; it appears in the Analyzer with its stop.

entries.say: echo, every 5 seconds, say the time, please
entries.does: A cadence: the intention runs on the clock; "echo, stop" rests it, "echo, restart intention 'every 5 seconds'" stands it again.

sections.title: How much of you a task needs — manual · manual assist · full auto
sections.lead: The kind of your ask decides how far the kernel goes without you, and it never goes one step further without a word from you. A THOUGHT moves nothing: you ask, one body answers, you are the whole loop (manual). An OBJECTIVE moves what you asked and stops at every consequence: the planner breaks it into steps, the crew acts, and any step that changes something holds for your Cancel or Yes (manual assist). An INTENTION keeps moving until you rest it: the kernel watches for what you named — a red watch, a clock — plans the next objective itself, files it, and the loop turns; you are told, not asked — except at a consequence, which still holds for you (full auto). Three things tell you which mode a thing is in: the chip under the composer (the kind), the hold row (the kernel is waiting on you), and the Analyzer (every intention and objective by origin, with its stop).

entries.say: what is the temperature outside?
entries.does: MANUAL. A thought: the librarian answers once, with its tools. Nothing in the world changes. Your part: the question.

entries.say: objective: get the weather tool healthy again
entries.does: MANUAL ASSIST. The planner writes the steps, the crew runs them, the Analyzer shows the tree. When a step would change something (retire, re-pin, refill), the chat shows a hold with Cancel as the default — nothing runs until you click Yes (a grave step asks for your authenticator's code). Your part: one word to start, one word at each hold. Say “stop it” at any time; what was left undone is said.

entries.say: keep this world resilient: when a watch goes red, get it green
entries.does: FULL AUTO. A standing purpose. The kernel observes (the red), reads the ground itself first — the watch, who it names and their state, the last acts on them, what happened last time — and hands the planner that dossier with the LEVERS it can pull (restart a body · check or restore a service or a mind · retire one); the planner answers with one lever and its reason; the kernel pulls it with its own hands, as a row in the intention’s session, then reads the watch again and says what happened — green after its act wears the cause, green on its own is said to be self-healed, still red tries once more and then hands you the dossier. You read it in the Analyzer (“last red: cured”) and the Intentions band; you are not asked. Consequential steps STILL hold for you: the kernel never lowers the ladder because it is running on its own. Your part: declare once; decide holds when they come; rest it when you want (“stop the … intention” — your code, then a master's click; “restart intention '…'” stands it again).

entries.say: echo, every 5 seconds, say the time, please
entries.does: FULL AUTO on a clock: the same loop, woken by a cadence instead of a red. “echo, stop” rests it.

entries.say: summon MITL · expected impact?
entries.does: In any mode, before you decide a hold: the Master Mind In The Loop says who and what the act touches, from the canon.

entries.say: (the light bulb)
entries.does: Manual: you act, the kernel answers. Manual assist: the kernel acts, you decide every consequence. Full auto: the kernel acts and plans, you still decide every consequence and can always stop. The kernel's reach grows with the kind you chose; your hand on the consequences never shrinks.

sections.title: When the kernel asks "Are you sure?"
sections.lead: A consequential act holds until you decide. Cancel is the default and has the focus; Yes needs a deliberate click.

entries.say: Cancel
entries.does: Nothing runs; the hold is recorded as cancelled.

entries.say: Yes — do it
entries.does: The act runs on your word and wears proof L2; a grave act asks for your authenticator's code instead ("enroll my authenticator" once).

entries.say: expected impact?
entries.does: MITL says who and what the act touches before you decide.

entries.say: (a proposal from a keeper)
entries.does: A keeper never retires, assigns, refills or re-pins alone — it proposes here and you cut; a proposal whose reason has passed withdraws itself.

sections.title: The Crew
sections.lead: Every body in this world, both sides: what it served and the job it runs. When this kernel seats the bodies itself (the Rust kernel alone), each card says where its process stands — alive, restarting, PARKED or refused. Beneath the bodies stands the shelf.

entries.say: what services are here? · show the tools · show the LLMs
entries.does: The shelf, from the registry: every tool, MCP server, store, source and LLM on one ladder — registered → versioned → healthy | unhealthy → retired.

entries.say: check the services · check the minds
entries.does: Every standing service probed by its kind; an LLM answers a one-token ping through the gateway.

entries.say: retire the weather tool · restore the weather tool
entries.does: Retire holds at the interlock; restore is a new fact. Retired is dormancy, never deletion.

entries.say: toolkeeper, add the MCP server at <command or URL>
entries.does: The server and its tools land on the shelf as identities; its secrets by env NAME only.

entries.say: stablekeeper, add the LLM ollama gemma3:270m as gemma
entries.does: An LLM wherever it lives — anthropic · openrouter · ollama · openai · compatible — becomes a stall in the Stable and an entry in the gateway; held for your yes.

entries.say: assign librarian to gemma · assign librarian to gemma for fast work · unassign librarian
entries.does: Which LLM a body uses, for all its work or one class of work (fast · standard · deep); the card says "LLM: …" and why.

entries.say: librarian's fuel · refill librarian by $2
entries.does: A body's allowance for this window and what it has spent; a refill holds at the interlock — real spending.

entries.say: schedule an ask for librarian… (on its card)
entries.does: A standing duty on the clock, shown on the card's job side; "rest it" stops it.

entries.say: restart the echo body
entries.does: A body the kernel PARKED (it died three times in five minutes) or refused at birth is tried again on your word — its deaths forgotten, the same self. A body that simply died comes back by itself; nothing is ever deleted.

sections.title: The Monitoring
sections.lead: The operating state of this world, live: the rails, the bodies, the asks, the watches, THE STABLE, the HEALTH CHECKS.

entries.say: watch for asks left waiting
entries.does: The monitor agent proposes a watch — a hold you cut; a watch is RED while its condition holds and turns in the chat.

entries.say: propose a watch that usd_today > 5
entries.does: A watch over the farm: spend today, thoughts per minute, LLMs standing, bodies out of fuel.

entries.say: HEALTH CHECKS
entries.does: What must be true of this world, read from the ground now: nine rows, each holds or BROKEN with its words; read every 30 seconds.

entries.say: run the harness against the librarian now
entries.does: The golden cases against a body's LLM; a failing run escalates to the chat. From the Rust kernel the run rides the rail to the body and lands when it is done.

entries.say: advance past parked 3
entries.does: The RAILS card names every event the dispatcher HOLDS at — bytes the rail carried that were never an envelope, or a fact that can never apply — parked with its evidence, nothing behind it dispatched until a person decides. Your word (or the card's lever) advances it, recorded in your name; nothing is lost silently and nothing loops.

sections.title: The Analyzer
sections.lead: Everything born in the chat, by origin: intentions, objectives, in flight and done. Every row is a door.

entries.say: (click a row)
entries.does: Its tree in words; an objective's row puts the chat in focus on it.

entries.say: stop the kernel's Resiliency intention
entries.does: A grave act: your code, then a declared master's click; the intention rests, recorded, never deleted.

entries.say: restart intention '<its words>'
entries.does: The reverse, through the same ladder; it "stands again".

sections.title: Your seat — who this door knows you are
sections.lead: Every door reads who you are from your SEAT, never from the page. You take a seat with the code your authenticator shows; it lasts a day. On a ground no one holds yet, the first person to prove an authenticator becomes its owner; from then on only the owner or a master can enroll someone new. Nobody types a master's name any more — a master confirms a grave act from their own seat, in their own window. Bodies hold the machine's twin: a LEASE, earned at the join desk — a body proves the key behind its DID, and a governing seat says yes.

entries.say: (the seat form) your name + the 6-digit code · Take my seat
entries.does: The kernel signs a token naming you, what you may do here and until when; the page carries it on every knock. The first proof on an unheld ground: “you hold this ground now”.

entries.say: (the seat form, no one holds the ground yet) your name · Enroll
entries.does: The QR for your authenticator; the first code finishes enrolling; the next one takes your seat as the owner.

entries.say: my seat · who am I seated as?
entries.does: Seated as whom, until when, and what the seat may do: retrieve · write (· govern for the owner and a master).

entries.say: leave my seat
entries.does: Ends this seat now — recorded, never deleted; the seat form returns. Another window's seat is its own.

entries.say: enroll quinn
entries.does: The owner's (or a master's) word: a QR for another person's authenticator; their first code finishes it here; they sit in their own browser with the next.

entries.say: enroll my authenticator
entries.does: Re-enrolling yourself is grave: your current code first, then the new QR.

entries.say: (a grave act, as the asker) type your code → a declared master clicks Confirm as master in THEIR window
entries.does: The two-person law, honestly: the master is a second seated person; the typed name is gone.

entries.say: who is at the door?
entries.does: The join desk: every body that asked to join this world, newest first — the crew (admitted on the crew manifest), a stranger waiting for your yes, one turned away. A stranger's knock appears in the chat as a hold: Cancel is the default; only the owner or a master can click Yes.

sections.title: You — what this ground knows about you
sections.lead: Your profile is yours: what you tell this ground about yourself, in your own words, labeled by who said it — “you told me” · “I observed” · “the mirror noticed” (reserved). Every body reads it first when it answers you; a routed ask carries it to the far cell for that answer alone. The YOU tag under the sun shows who this door knows you are.

entries.say: my name is JB · call me JB
entries.does: Your name, trusted on your word. The newest word wins; the old one stays in the record.

entries.say: I live in Boulder, Colorado · my place is Payson, Arizona
entries.does: Your place, in your words. The kernel looks its coordinates and clock up once (Open-Meteo, no key) and keeps them beside your words as “I observed” — the weather tool then answers for YOUR place, never a fixed point. With no place told, it says so rather than reading someone else's weather.

entries.say: my time zone is America/Denver · my clock is Europe/Paris
entries.does: Your clock, told; every time a body reads you is in it. Untold, the clock of your told place; untold both, the browser's zone, then the ground's dial.

entries.say: remember about me: I take my coffee black
entries.does: A free word about you. Every resident reads it in its context, never recites it unasked.

entries.say: what do you know about me? · show my profile · who am I
entries.does: The portrait: every live word with its label and the clock this ground would use for you.

entries.say: forget about me: my place · forget my name · forget that I take my coffee black
entries.does: A recorded withdrawal on your word — the words no longer read; the record keeps that you said them once. Never a deletion.

sections.title: Memory, sessions and the export
sections.lead: The kernel never forgets: every word acquired is kept verbatim with its lineage; a correction is a sibling, never an overwrite.

entries.say: what do you remember about the trailer?
entries.does: Recall, stemmed and ranked; the librarian answers from the Record, word for word.

entries.say: list my sessions
entries.does: Each session's short version — the digest — written from the Record alone; the same on every door.

entries.say: export compliance for this session · export compliance for today
entries.does: Signed by the kernel's own self (did:orreth:kernel:…); a stranger can verify the chain and the signature.

entries.say: forget the trailer note
entries.does: Governed erasure: every version leaves; a tombstone keeps the hashes; the digests that cited it are rebuilt.

sections.title: Cells — a second universe, and the seam between them
sections.lead: A cell is one universe's home: its own kernel, its own database and role, its own benches, its own bodies and keys. Two cells that name each other can speak over a signed seam. What this world is and where it stands reads in the Monitoring's PULSE and PEERS.

entries.say: what world is this?
entries.does: The universe, the cell it stands in, its epoch, and the peers it names.

entries.say: librarian@two, what is the weather?
entries.does: An ask that names a cell ROUTES HOME: cell two's own librarian answers, and the answer lands on your ask here, its journey saying so. "two/librarian, …" works too.

entries.say: stop it (on a routed ask's line)
entries.does: Rests the ask here and tells its home cell to rest it too — the human can always stop what the machine manages.

entries.say: scripts/dev.sh cell two (in a terminal)
entries.does: Lights a second universe, u:two, on its own database and role, sealed from this one; relight this kernel so it names cell two as a peer (SPINE_PEERS).

entries.say: re-home this universe to cell three
entries.does: Consequential: held at the interlock (your yes). The universe's epoch advances; this kernel then refuses to serve it, and a peer still wearing the old epoch is told to re-hear the world.

entries.say: (when a peer is dark)
entries.does: An ask routed to it reads PARKED in plain words — nothing is lost; the moment the peer answers again the ask goes and is answered once. The PEERS view says "unreachable since".
